turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: Hello. Well, I'm here because of this scar on my wrist. I know it's probably not as bad as it looks to me, but it's really been bothering me. When I’m at church, or sitting down to play bridge, I just keep feeling like everyone’s eyes go right to it. It just feels like it’s the very first thing they notice about me now, and I can't seem to shake that feeling.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes a persistent preoccupation with a scar on their wrist, acknowledging it is likely not as noticeable to others as it feels to them, yet believing others focus directly on it.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself thinking about the scar often, even when you're trying not to?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I really do. Like I was just saying, I try to remind myself that it's probably not as bad as it looks to me, but I just can't stop focusing on it. I'll be trying to pay attention to the sermon at church, or focusing on my cards at bridge, and my mind just goes right back to it. I get so distracted by the feeling that everyone's eyes are glued to my wrist, and I just can't seem to turn that thought off, no matter how hard I try.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient confirms an intrusive, persistent preoccupation with a perceived physical defect (a scar on her wrist), stating she cannot stop focusing on it and feels unable to turn the thought off despite trying.

turns.doctor_question: Does this preoccupation with your scar ever make it hard for you to function normally—like affecting your sleep, mood, or ability to enjoy activities you used to like?
turns.patient_response: Yes, it definitely has. I work as a bookkeeping clerk, and lately, I've actually been late turning in some of my work. I just get so caught up trying to figure out how to hide it or make sure it won't be noticed. And... it's affected my free time, too. I volunteer with the church choir and at the local theater, but I've skipped some of those commitments recently because I just couldn't face people. I spend so much time worrying about my wrist that it just gets in the way of doing the things I need to do.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient reports spending an excessive amount of time worrying about their wrist scar to the point that it interferes with work and activities, confirming a preoccupation with a perceived physical flaw.
symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient describes getting caught up trying to figure out how to hide the scar or make sure it is not noticed, demonstrating appearance-related camouflaging behaviors.

turns.doctor_question: Has the worry about your scar ever made you avoid social situations altogether, or caused you a lot of emotional distress even when you're alone?
turns.patient_response: Well, I haven't completely stopped going out or anything like that. I still go to work and try to keep up with things. But it definitely causes me distress, yes. Even when I'm just sitting at home by myself, I find myself looking at it, worrying about how it looks. It just makes me feel very down and anxious, even when there's nobody around to see it.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient reports persistent worry and distress regarding the appearance of their scar, frequently looking at it and feeling anxious even when alone.

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever feel that the scar looks different than it actually does, or that it has some unusual or special meaning that others might not understand?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't think so. It doesn't mean anything special or unusual. It's just a scar. I mean, I know exactly what it is, and I don't think it's changing shape or anything like that. I just... I just think it looks terrible. So, no, there's no hidden meaning to it, I just really hate how noticeable it is.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient explicitly denies that the scar has any special, unusual, or hidden meaning, or that it is changing shape, ruling out delusional interpretations.
